person-caseyneistat.name: Casey Neistat
person-caseyneistat.headline: ModRetro
person-caseyneistat.summary:
YouTuber mostly.  Filmmaking has been the throughline for my career as a founder, technologist, marketer, journalist and educator.

started making videos as a teenager then

Founded NSA, Neistat Scott & Associates, in 2007.  NSA was a production company specializing in advertising, documentaries and television.  The NSA production 'The Neistat Brothers' was an 8 episode series my brother Van and I wrote and directed, the series was sold to HBO in 2008.  Another NSA highlight was the narrative feature film 'Daddy Long Legs' directed by Josh and Benny Safdie which premiered at the Cannes Film Festival in 2009 and distributed by IFC.

Casey Neistat LLC was created in 2010, a commercial production company solely focused on advertising.  CN LLC did work for myriad clients including Nike, Google, Starbucks.

In 2013 I was granted a fellowship at the MIT Media Lab working under proffessor Sep Kamvar's Social Computing Group.  After completing this residency I returned to NYC and founded my first venture backed startup, a software development company called Beme.

Beme was aquired by Turner Broadcasting System in 2016.

In 2015 I shifted my filmmaking to YouTube creating a daily show, 'The Vlog'.  The Vlog garnered a lot of attention growing my YouTube channel from under 300k subcribers to over 10million in the first 18 months of its production.  Viewership totals were over 3 billion.  The Vlog also won a number of awards including 'YouTuber of the Year', 'Creator of the Year', GQ's 'Man of the Year' and a bunch more that I would feel silly listing here.

I live in NYC, have 3 kids and am married.  this about page was not written by ai.

person-reshmasaujani.summary: Reshma Saujani is a leading activist, the founder of Girls Who Code, the founder and CEO of Moms First, and the host of My So-Called Midlife with Lemonada Media. She has spent more than a decade building movements to fight for women and girls’ economic empowerment, working to close the gender gap in the tech sector, and most recently fighting for the structural changes moms need and deserve including affordable child care and paid leave. She is a New York Times bestselling author of several books including PAY UP: The Future of Women and Work (And Why It’s Different Than You Think), Brave, Not Perfect, and the Girls Who Code book series. As a leading voice on women’s empowerment, her 2023 Smith College Commencement speech on imposter syndrome has more than 18 million views, and her influential TED talk, “Teach girls bravery, not perfection,” has more than 54 million views globally. In 2024, she launched My So-Called Midlife, a podcast with Lemonada Media that quickly entered Apple’s Top 10 show chart, reached #1 in Health and Fitness, and was named one of the best new podcasts of the year by TIME magazine. Reshma began her career as an attorney and Democratic organizer. In 2010, she surged onto the political scene as the first Indian American woman to run for U.S. Congress. Reshma lives in New York City with her husband, Nihal, their sons, Shaan and Sai, and their dog Steve.

person-6ghz.role: Host & Creator — Inner Garden Podcast: Stories of Healing, Land & Legacy
person-6ghz.headline: Founder Black Girls CODE | Founder & CEO Black Innovation Lab and Ascend Ventures | Investor | Author of Ascending | Systems Architect Exploring Power, Innovation & Cultural Transformation
person-6ghz.summary:
🧩 Coined "Black Girlboss Paradox" — a framework exploring the intersection of race, gender, leadership, and power.
 
I build systems, stories, and platforms that expand who gets to shape the future. My work sits at the intersection of technology, equity, cultural power, and transformation.
 
As the founder of Black Girls CODE, I built one of the most influential STEM movements of the last decade, introducing more than 100,000 girls of color to coding, creativity, and community. Today, through Black Innovation Lab by Ascend Ventures, I’m building a venture ecosystem designed to support visionary founders creating solutions that shape a more equitable and expansive future.

I’m also the founder of Roots & Resilience Studio, home to Inner Garden: Stories of Healing, Land & Legacy and the Roots & Resilience Substack, where I explore Black women's leadership journeys through their connection to land, memory, and narrative.
 
I’ve been honored by the White House and the Smithsonian for my contributions to technology and social impact. My current work focuses on building frameworks and platforms that center innovation, sustainability, ownership, and the leadership of Black women.
 
Across my work, I explore how power operates and how new systems can be built with equity, imagination, and accountability at the center through investing, strategic advising, ecosystem building, storytelling, and public speaking.
 
I’m especially passionate about supporting founders, executives, and emerging leaders, particularly Black women navigating systems not originally designed for us to thrive.
 
If you’re building transformative systems, investing in inclusive innovation, or reimagining leadership and cultural power, let’s connect.

person-simonsinek.location: New York, New York, United States
person-simonsinek.summary:
Simon Sinek is an unshakable optimist who believes in a bright future and our ability to build it together. Simon's WHY is to inspire people to do what inspires them so that, together, each of us can change our world for the better.

With a vision to change the way businesses think, act, and operate, Simon and his team work with leaders and organizations in nearly every industry to help transform company culture and create a better working world.

As a trained ethnographer, Simon has discovered remarkable patterns about how the greatest leaders and organizations think, act, and communicate. He is fascinated by the people and organizations that make the greatest, lasting impact on the world. He has devoted his life to sharing his thinking, and leading a movement to inspire people to do the things that inspire them.

Simon may be best known for popularizing the concept of WHY in his first Ted Talk in 2009. It has since become one of the most watched talks of all time on TED.com, with 37+ million views. 

Simon is a bestselling author and shares his ideas in the books Start With Why, Leaders Eat Last, Together Is Better, Find Your Why, and The Infinite Game.

Learn more at simonsinek.com.
